channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Comissão aciona PGR contra Mauro Vieira por falta em audiência
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies’ Foreign Relations Committee voted to file a crime report with the Attorney General’s Office against Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira for unjustifiably missing a summoned hearing on the U.S. classification of Brazilian criminal groups as terrorists. Vieira instead met with President Lula to discuss U.S. threats of 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods, a negotiation deadline that expired that same day. The committee deemed the Itamaray’s explanation evasive, affirmed his legal duty to attend, and rescheduled his appearance for August.

item.title: Aprovação de Lula supera numericamente desaprovação pela 1ª vez desde 2024
item.description: The Quaest poll shows President Lula's approval rating at 48%, surpassing disapproval at 47% for the first time since December 2023, marking a technical tie. This reverses a previous trend where disapproval led by as much as nine points in April, indicating a gradual improvement in public perception, with a margin of error of two percentage points.

item.title: Os cinco sinais de alerta para Flávio Bolsonaro em nova pesquisa
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows a decline in Flávio Bolsonaro's spontaneous voting intention, dropping from 17% in June to 14% this month, with significant losses among non-bolsonarist right-wing voters (from 44% to 32%) and bolsonarists (from 50% to 45%). His rejection rose to 57%, while 54% of voters no longer see him as more moderate than his father, and more people fear the return of the Bolsonaro family (46%) than Lula's re-election (38%).

item.title: Quaest: Lula tem 45% e abre oito pontos de vantagem sobre Flávio Bolsonaro no 2º turn
item.description: Quaest poll shows Lula with 45% voting intentions in a runoff, eight points ahead of Flávio Bolsonaro (37%), increasing his lead from six points in June. The family feud between Flávio and Michelle Bolsonaro, along with the PF operation against Jaques Wagner, negatively affected the senator’s image. For the first time since December 2023, Lula’s government approval exceeds disapproval in the survey.

item.title: Incoerente e preso à bolha, Flávio patina na pré-campanha e terá de rever estratégias
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows Lula leading Flávio Bolsonaro in a hypothetical second-round runoff with 45% to 37%. Flávio remains confined to his Bolsonarist base, losing ground among independent voters and exhibiting high voter volatility, with only 62% of his supporters saying their choice is definitive. His pre-campaign faces criticism for incoherence: attempting to appear moderate while maintaining radical rhetoric, causing discomfort even among allies.

item.title: A família Bolsonaro nos condena a mais quatro anos de Lula e PT
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is falling further behind Lula, with 37% of voting intentions in the runoff compared to Lula's 45%, according to the Genial/Quaest poll. His rejection rate rose to 57%, while Lula's dropped to 50%, indicating voters fear a Bolsonaro return more than Lula's continuation. Even non-Bolsonarist right-wing voters reduced their support for Flávio from 82% to 74%.

item.title: Quaest: Lula percebeu que Brasil não se divide só entre ricos e pobres
item.description: President Lula's approval rating has surpassed disapproval for the first time since December 2024, with 48% approving and 47% disapproving, according to the Genial/Quaest poll. This marks a modest recovery in his public image after months of decline. The excerpt suggests Lula has recognized that Brazil's divisions extend beyond a simple rich-poor dichotomy.

item.title: Renan Santos acusa Quaest de divulgar pesquisa com “inconsistências”
item.description: Presidential pre-candidate Renan Santos criticized Quaest's latest poll, accusing the institute of releasing results full of 'inconsistencies' and questioning its methodology. He expressed surprise that Quaest had stopped conducting internal surveys, suggesting this undermines the credibility of the data.

item.title: Petistas veem perda de credibilidade de Flávio e acertos de Lula após pesquisa Genial/Quaest
item.description: Members of Lula's (PT) re-election campaign say the new Genial/Quaest poll shows a growing loss of credibility for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) among voters, indicating difficulties for the opposition candidate to gain traction. The assessment suggests Lula maintains an advantage in perceived reliability and accuracy of proposals, reinforcing his position in the 2026 electoral race.

item.title: STF chega a 5 votos para anular doação de fiel à Igreja Universal
item.description: The Federal Supreme Court has secured five votes to uphold a ruling requiring the Universal Church of the Kingdom of God to refund donations made by a faithful member, deemed the result of irresistible moral coercion and abuse of right. Minister Dias Toffoli joined rapporteur Edson Fachin and ministers Cármen Lúcia, Alexandre de Moraes, and Cristiano Zanin in this stance, as the virtual plenary judgment continues until August 5. The original TJ-MG ruling ordered the IURD to return R$229,100 with interest and adjustment, plus R$12,000 for moral damages.

item.title: Gasto milionário de institutos com pesquisas autofinanciadas cresce e divide setor
item.description: The use of self-funded resources by polling institutes for electoral surveys has significantly increased in the first half of 2026, with R$23.4 million invested and 46.3% of all surveys registered with the TSE being self-financed — nearly five times the amount in 2022. The practice divides the sector: critics, such as João Francisco Meira of Abep, claim it may conceal real funders and advocate for its prohibition and strict TSE oversight, while defenders, like Márcia Cavallari of Ipsos-Ipec, argue it can be legitimate in exceptional cases but warn against it becoming the norm.

item.title: Quaest: Flávio Bolsonaro perde apoio na direita não bolsonarista
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro lost support among non-bolsonarista right-wing voters, dropping from 74% in May to 54% currently, according to Quaest research. His support among bolsonaristas remains stable above 90%. The decline is linked to the 'Dark Horse' case, involving alleged illegal financing of a film about Jair Bolsonaro by Daniel Vorcaro.

item.title: Ibovespa cai com tarifaço, eleições e dados do setor de serviços
item.description: The Ibovespa fell 0.4% on Wednesday (15), pressured by uncertainty over U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods, the 2026 presidential election showing Lula with an eight-point lead over Flávio Bolsonaro, and weaker-than-expected services sector data, which declined 0.4% in May. Investors are reducing equity exposure while awaiting the U.S. tariff announcement, due today. The MDIC reiterated that the proposed 25% (Section 301) and 12.5% (forced labor) tariffs are unjust and do not support a mutually adequate bilateral agreement.

item.title: Crusoé: Flavinho paz e amor ainda não convence brasileiros
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro launched his pre-candidacy in December aiming to present himself as a more moderate version of his father and brothers, emphasizing his Bolsonaro principles while rejecting violence. Despite this effort to soften his image, the strategy has yet to convince Brazilian voters, who remain skeptical about his candidacy.

item.title: Carlos Portinho é escolhido pré-candidato ao Senado pelo PL no Rio de Janeiro
item.description: Senator Carlos Portinho (PL-RJ) was officially named the pre-candidate for re-election by the Liberal Party in Rio de Janeiro, announcing his bid to retain his Senate seat in 2026. His selection completes the party’s state ticket, which already includes Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) as the pre-candidate for President of Brazil. The announcement was made on Tuesday, June 14, and underscores the PL’s strategy to strengthen its electoral base in Rio de Janeiro ahead of the 2026 general elections.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro pode ser multado em até R$ 25.000 por carta do pai
item.description: The campaign of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) may face a fine of up to R$25,000 by the TSE if the dissemination of a handwritten letter from jailed former president Jair Bolsonaro is deemed premature electoral propaganda. The letter, read during a social media live by Flávio, urged support for his presidential bid and was analyzed for violating campaign timing rules. Electoral prosecutor Alexandre Espinosa will assess whether the act constitutes an violation of the August 15 campaign start date under Brazilian electoral law.

item.title: Resultado de pesquisa eleitoral aumenta incertezas no mercado
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows Lula leading against Flávio Bolsonaro, but the Senate's approval of PEC 14, which grants earlier retirement to community health agents, raises fiscal concerns due to its estimated R$30 billion impact over ten years. Economists warn that regardless of who wins in 2026, the next president will face a challenging fiscal environment, with permanent spending lacking proper financing. Electoral uncertainty remains due to scandals and noise in both candidates' trajectories, while current fiscal policy distances Brazil from investment-grade status.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro lança plano para tentar romper resistência feminina
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro will launch the 'Brasil por Elas' plan to attract female voters, proposing cashback for unpaid care work, expanded credit for women entrepreneurs, and financial independence incentives. The initiative aims to overcome his electoral disadvantage against Lula, worsened by conflicts with Michelle Bolsonaro and controversial remarks from allies. The presentation will feature Daniella Marques, former Caixa president, and his wife Fernanda Bolsonaro.

item.title: 'Eleição não se elege pelos rejeitados', diz Caiado sobre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro na pesquisa Quaest
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), pre-candidate for President, criticized the polarization between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, stating that 'an election is not won by the rejected,' following a Quaest poll showing his support rising from 3% to 4%. He argued both leaders are 'playing the same game' and not concerned with Brazil, emphasizing the need to discuss economy, security, education, infrastructure, and foreign relations. Caiado also thanked Paraná Governor Ratinho Junior (PSD) for his support, noting their past healthy rivalry as an asset to his campaign.

item.title: Meio-Dia em Brasília: Todo mundo odeia a pesquisa Quaest
item.description: The Meio-Dia em Brasília program discusses the latest Quaest poll on the 2026 electoral race, which has faced criticism from the opposition to Lula’s government over its methodology. The segment also covers expectations surrounding Donald Trump’s proposed tariff policies and their potential effects on Brazil.

item.title: Nikolas rebate fala de Janja e critica PL da Misoginia
item.description: Federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) rebutted first lady Janja's statement that the nickname 'gastadeira' constitutes misogyny and renewed his criticism of the Misogyny Bill, saying he continues to work to block its vote in the Chamber. He argued the bill is a narrative seeking to control speech and that criticizing Janja's spending or the bill itself is labeled as misogyny. The remarks came in plenary session, two days after Janja's interview with Uol, amid efforts by rapporteur Tabata Amaral to secure a vote before the parliamentary recess.

item.title: O recado de Lula à campanha sobre as pesquisas eleitorais
item.description: President Lula instructed his pre-campaign team not to react to election polls, noting that the approximately 80 days remaining until the election is a long time in political terms. He warned against both euphoria over favorable results and defeatism over unfavorable ones, stressing the need to focus on campaign work. The Quaest Genial/Quaest poll shows Lula leading with a 12-point advantage in the first round and an 8-point lead in the second round against Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Crusoé: Renan alerta para “terra arrasada” pelo Congresso
item.description: Renan Santos, pre-candidate for president from the Mission party, warned that Congress is destroying public finances by approving special retirement for health agents, leaving a 'scorched earth' for the next government. He said that, as he expects to win the election, he will have to deal with the fiscal hole left by the current legislature.

item.title: Dino intima presidentes de partidos sobre destinação de emendas
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino ordered party leaders with congressional representation to disclose, within 10 days, details on the definition, management, distribution, or operationalization of parliamentary amendments, following statements by PL president Valdemar Costa Neto acknowledging interference in amendment allocation. The measure aims to ensure transparency and traceability, citing suspicious amendments linked to politicians without mandates, such as Valdemar and former deputy Eduardo Cunha.

item.title: Mesmo convocado, Mauro Vieira falta à comissão na Câmara
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira missed a scheduled hearing before the Chamber of Deputies' Foreign Relations and National Defense Committee, despite being summoned to discuss the risk of U.S. military intervention in Brazil. The Itamaraty cited a prior meeting with President Lula and claimed to have formally requested a postponement, but deputies proceeded with the session. Deputy Marcel van Hatten accused Vieira of committing a crime of responsibility due to his absence and vague communication.

item.title: Leia a íntegra da nova pesquisa Quaest sobre a eleição presidencial
item.description: The Quaest poll released on July 15, 2026 shows Lula leading the presidential race with 40% in the first round, 12 points ahead of Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) at 28%. In a simulated runoff, Lula would win with 45% against Bolsonaro's 37%. Approval of Lula's government stands at 48%, compared to 47% disapproval, indicating a technical tie.

item.title: Ao vivo: Câmara discute tarifas, política externa e facções criminosas
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies holds a public hearing to discuss Brazil's foreign policy under Lula, focusing on tensions with the U.S., including potential new tariffs and claims of possible U.S. military intervention. Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira was invited but did not attend, while the government asserts it sees a risk of U.S. action and the Itamaraty faces criticism for not explaining its assessments. The debate also includes a proposal to classify criminal factions as terrorist organizations.

item.title: Dino manda presidentes de partidos explicarem emendas após fala de Valdemar
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino has given a 10-day deadline for party presidents to provide information on the definition, management, distribution, or operationalization of parliamentary amendments by party leaderships. The order follows statements by Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the PL party, which raised concerns about transparency in the use of public funds. The measure aims to ensure that amendments are applied in accordance with the law and under judicial oversight.

item.title: Dino determina que presidentes dos 21 partidos com cadeiras no Congresso expliquem se têm 'cotas' para indicar emendas
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino has ordered the leaders of 21 parties with congressional representation to explain within ten days whether they use 'quotas' or other mechanisms for distributing parliamentary amendments. The ruling aims to prevent the 'outsourcing' and 'privatization' of amendments, which are prohibited by law, and requires detailed information on the nature, authorization, legal basis, and procedures of such mechanisms. Affected parties include the PT, PL, União Brasil, and PSD, with leaders such as Edinho Silva, Valdemar Costa Neto, Ciro Nogueirazado, with party presidents like Edinho Silva, Valdemar Costa Neto, Ciro Nogueira, and Gilberto Kassab required to provide clarifications.

item.title: O estado onde o PT é favorito ao Planalto, mas peleja para reeleger governador
item.description: In Ceará, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) holds a commanding lead in presidential re-election polls for 2026, outperforming Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) by over 40 percentage points in both rounds. However, in the gubernatorial race, Governor Elmano de Freitas (PT) is technically tied with former governor Ciro Gomes (PSDB), with differences falling within the 2-point margin of error, highlighting a PT popularity paradox in the state.

item.title: Vantagem de Lula na Quaest preocupa aliados de Flávio, e campanha aposta em reação com o fim do pacote de benesses do governo
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows Lula with 45% voting intentions versus 37% for Flávio Bolsonaro in a potential runoff, with the senator's rejection rising to 57%, making him the most rejected candidate. PL allies attribute the decline to a cascade of crises since May, including the Dark Horse scandal, internal criticism, a rift with Michelle Bolsonaro, and backlash over his U.S. trip during U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods, urging Flávio to strengthen dialogue with party leaders and show more humility.

item.title: Partidos reclamam de plataformas digitais por propaganda de produtos em evento do TSE
item.description: Political parties complained that digital platforms such as TikTok, Meta, X, Kwai, Google, YouTube, and Telegram used a TSE virtual workshop to promote their products instead of clarifying doubts about social media use during the electoral campaign. Although the event was organized at the parties' request to understand platform functionalities and electoral rules, advisors criticized the shift to commercial focus, with complaints recorded in the event chat. Despite the criticism, some sources noted that, as the meeting was voluntary, platform product promotion could be expected.

item.title: Bolsonaro deve esclarecer descumprimento de cautelares até esta 4ª
item.description: Bolsonaro's defense has until Wednesday (Jul 15, 2026) to respond to Minister Alexandre de Moraes regarding a possible breach of precautionary measures, following the disclosure of a handwritten letter attributed to the former president by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro on Instagram. Moraes suspended visits between father and son for 90 days and activated the Electoral Public Ministry to investigate potential premature electoral propaganda, as the letter designated Flávio as Bolsonaro's spokesperson in the 2026 presidential race. Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year-and-3-month sentence under house arrest for humanitarian health reasons after being convicted of leading a coup attempt in 2022.

item.title: O que aponta Quaest sobre a reação dos eleitores ao vídeo de Michelle Bolsonaro contra Flávio
item.description: Quaest poll shows 51% of voters were unaware of Michelle Bolsonaro's videos against Flávio Bolsonaro. Among those aware, 45% believe she was right to publish the videos, compared to 38% who think she was wrong; 31% consider her statements totally true and 27% partially true. The main attributed motive was her desire to run for president in Flávio's place (34%), and 47% believe her direct involvement would not boost the PL pre-candidate's electoral chances.

item.title: Na expectativa de tarifaço, Flávio culpa Lula e diz: "Fui lá negociar"
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro accused Lula of provoking the U.S. and contributing to the threatened 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, stating that he himself went to the U.S. to negotiate and avoid the measure. He also advocated for delaying or canceling the tariffs, arguing that their imposition before the elections would politically benefit Lula.

item.title: ‘Duelo de rejeições’: a má notícia para Flávio Bolsonaro na nova pesquisa Genial/Quaest
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro’s rejection rose from 52% to 57%, while Lula’s fell from 55% to 50%, reversing their previous dynamic. Flávio now leads in rejection by 7 points — outside the poll’s margin of error. Contributing factors include allegations of irregular funding for a film about his father, a public rift with Michelle Bolsonaro, and an ineffective U.S. visit amid new Trump tariffs.

item.title: Mauro Vieira não comparece a audiência na Câmara sobre PCC e CV
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira did not attend a Chamber of Deputies hearing on Brazil's foreign policy regarding the U.S. designation of PCC and CV as terrorist groups, citing a scheduling conflict with a meeting with President Lula. The committee had approved his summons to discuss risks of extraterritorial U.S. military action, with Vieira proposing to reschedule for August.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro precisa recuperar espaço na direita não-bolsonarista e entre independentes, avaliam aliados após Quaest
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro needs to regain support among non-Bolsonarist right-wing voters and independents after losing trust due to his proximity to banker Daniel Vorcaro. Although he retains strong backing from Bolsonarist hardliners (91%), his standing among moderate voters is eroding, with undecided voters rising from 3% to 11%. The Quaest poll indicates he remains the PL’s only viable candidate to challenge Lula in a potential runoff.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: Michelle tem mais apoio em embate com Flávio, e maioria acha que Wagner está errado
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows 45% of Brazilians believe Michelle Bolsonaro was right in her criticisms of her stepson Flávio Bolsonaro, compared to 38% who think she was wrong, although 51% were unaware of the video. Regarding Senator Jaques Wagner (PT-BA), 54% were unaware of the PF operation in the Master case, but among those informed, most view his actions as incorrect. The electoral impact of these issues remains limited due to low public awareness.

item.title: Michelle convenceu muito mais gente do que Flávio
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll showed that former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro convinced more people than her stepson, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), amid their public rift. While Lula leads further ahead of Flávio in the 2026 presidential race, Michelle’s desabafo video reached 49% of respondents, indicating broader impact. This confirms prior trends suggesting Michelle has greater electoral persuasion power than Flávio in the current political landscape.

item.title: Lula fez cartas e recebeu Haddad 21 vezes na prisão, mas não tinha condenação no STF e restrições como as de Bolsonaro
item.description: Lula received Haddad 21 times in prison in 2018, during which he orchestrated his candidacy through letters, despite lacking a final conviction under the Clean Record Law. Unlike Bolsonaro, whose father's visit was restricted by Moraes in 2026, Lula had free access as a lawyer and maintained political activity until being replaced by Haddad. The comparison overlooks legal differences: Lula was imprisoned after a second-instance conviction, while Bolsonaro has not yet exhausted appeals.

item.title: Michelle tem apoio de 42% em disputa com Flávio Bolsonaro, diz Quaest
item.description: A Quaest poll shows 42% of respondents support Michelle Bolsonaro in her dispute with stepson Flávio Bolsonaro, compared to 18% backing the senator. The conflict, involving allegations of mistreatment by Flávio, unfolded ahead of the 2026 elections and highlights divisions within the Bolsonaro-aligned right, with Michelle having been previously considered for the presidency before Flávio was selected as the PL's presidential candidate.

item.title: Maioria dos eleitores avalia que Flávio não é mais moderado que a família Bolsonaro, aponta Genial/Quaest
item.description: A majority of voters (54%) believe Flávio Bolsonaro is no longer more moderate than his family, up four points since June. His image as a 'moderate Bolsonaro' has declined from 39% in April to 29% currently, while 57% of Brazilians know him and would not vote for him. Additionally, 46% fear the return of the Bolsonaros to power, compared to 38% who fear Lula’s re-election.

item.title: Áudio: Senado aprova MP do Frete Mínimo, que beneficia caminhoneiros
item.description: The Senate approved Provisional Measure 1.343/2026, which mandates the registration of road cargo transport operations and strengthens enforcement of the minimum freight floor, benefiting truck drivers. The measure, now headed for presidential sanction, also includes a pardon for drivers who blocked roads after the 2022 elections, approved with amendments by lawmakers.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: para 45%, Michelle acertou em gravar vídeo contra Flávio; 38% consideram erro
item.description: A Genial/Quaest poll shows 45% of voters believed Michelle Bolsonaro was right to publicly disclose her disagreement with Flávio Bolsonaro, while 38% thought it was a mistake. 17% did not know or declined to answer.

item.title: O eleitorado que puxou a aprovação de Lula ao mais alto patamar do ano, segundo pesquisa
item.description: Lula reached 48% approval in July 2026, his highest level this year and the highest since December 2025, with steady growth since April. The largest gain came from the highest-income group (above five minimum wages), which saw a 6-point approval increase and a 6-point disapproval drop in one month. Young voters (16-34) added 5 points in approval and reduced disapproval by 4, while the South — despite remaining the most critical region — rose 4 points in approval and fell 5 in disapproval since June.

item.title: Cid Gomes aparece à frente na disputa pelo Senado no Ceará
item.description: Senator Cid Gomes (PSB-CE) leads the Senate reelection race in Ceará with 26% voter intention, according to a Real Time Big Data poll, closely followed by Capitão Wagner (União Brasil) at 22%, within the margin of error. Gomes decided to run again at the request of President Lula (PT), while Wagner tops a second scenario without Gomes, showing strong competitiveness between the two main contenders.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: 42% concordam mais com Michelle em briga com Flávio
item.description: A Genial/Quaest poll shows 42% of respondents side more with Michelle Bolsonaro after her public dispute with Flávio Bolsonaro, versus 18% supporting the senator. The conflict, stemming from disagreements over the PL’s electoral slate in Ceará, led Michelle to resign from PL Women’s leadership and sparked divided opinions: 45% believe she was right to release the video, while 38% think she was wrong.

item.title: Flávio é rejeitado por 57% e Lula, por 50%, diz Quaest
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) has a 57% rejection rate, while President Lula (PT) has 50%, according to a Quaest poll released on July 15, 2026. The survey, conducted between July 10–13 with 2,004 respondents across 120 municipalities, has a 2-point margin of error and was funded by Banco Genial in partnership with Globo Group.

item.title: A vitória da ala política do PL sobre o ‘bolsonarismo raiz’
item.description: The selection of Carlos Portinho (PL-RJ) for the Senate race represented a victory for the political wing of the PL over the 'bolsonarism raiz' faction, defeating the Bolsonaro family's favored candidate, Carlos Jordy (PL-RJ). The state party directory, backed by over 30 inland mayors, prioritized electoral viability to bolster the presidential bid of Flávio Bolsonaro and the gubernatorial campaign of Douglas Ruas, favoring pragmatic alliances over pure ideological alignment.
